requirements.title: One sequence cannot repeat the same storage unit
requirements.definition: EQUIVALENCE cannot force one storage unit to occupy two positions of a storage sequence. Sharing units across different sequences is the intended facility; the forbidden condition is repetition inside a sequence, possibly caused transitively by several sets.

pending.two-positions-one-scalar: PENDING prose-policy/source pair: ordinary INTEGER a(2),b,c; sets (a(1),b),(a(2),b) force a's positions1 and2 to be the same unit. Repair only the second b occurrence to c. All indices, types, bounds and object roles are independently legal. Require a repeated-unit/contradictory-offset cause, not a grammar or unsupported-feature failure.
pending.transitive-repeated-position: PENDING prose-policy/source pair: ordinary INTEGER a(2),b,c,d; sets (a(1),b),(b,c),(a(2),c). Replace only the last c by d. Trace the three equalities to the repetition in a; retain the intermediate objects and declarations in the control.
pending.consistent-transitive-control: PENDING compile/source positive control with ordinary INTEGER a,b,c and sets (a,b),(b,c),(a,c). Repeated relationships are consistent here and do not put one unit into two positions of a multiunit sequence. No new runtime effect or automatic diagnostic obligation follows from this control.
pending.overlapping-predicates-gate: PENDING source qualification records interaction with p2 and 19.5.3.3. Some contradictory offset systems violate both restrictions; do not manufacture two uniquely isolated diagnostic causes or a reuse edge. Coordinator must adjudicate the actual finite source witness and any diagnostic-policy ownership.

requirements.oracle: Finite source-level unit/offset equations and source-minimal conforming controls, with all object, type, constant-index and scope predicates already valid. A reported contradiction may be considered only under a separately adjudicated context or diagnostic policy. Compile admission of a consistent control and failure of an inconsistent input are not, by themselves, a standard-mandated diagnostic oracle.
requirements.oracle_limitation: These are unnumbered restrictions, not automatic4.2 numbered-rule reporting duties. The current case contract requires an explicit lfortran-policy basis for a prospective prose diagnostic. Any independently applicable numbered/context obligation must be proved separately. Do not demand fatal rejection or a printed S/rule code. No runtime values are taken from a contradictory association. Unsupported facilities, arbitrary diagnostic keywords, crashes, resources and unrelated errors cannot qualify a semantic report; all source/control mechanisms remain pending.

requirements.title: Consecutive units cannot be mapped nonconsecutively
requirements.definition: The associations specified by EQUIVALENCE must preserve consecutive storage-unit relationships. They cannot prescribe gaps or reversal for units that are consecutive in a sequence. All relevant sequences and alignments, including transitive ones, must be considered.

pending.gapped-alignment: PENDING prose-policy/source pair: INTEGER a(2),b(3); sets (a(1),b(1)),(a(2),b(3)). Source equations try to map consecutive a positions to separated b positions. Change only b(3) to b(2) for the consistent control.19.5.3.3 also exposes a repeated-unit contradiction, so p1 can be coupled; no exclusive p2 diagnostic is promised.
pending.reversed-alignment: PENDING prose-policy/source pair: INTEGER a(2),b(3); sets (a(1),b(2)),(a(2),b(1)). Repair only the second b(1) to b(3), preserving a forward shifted overlap. Qualify all constant bounds and explain the reversed-versus-consecutive equations; never execute the inconsistent negative for value evidence.
pending.transitive-gap: PENDING prose-policy/source pair: INTEGER a(2),b(3),x,y; sets (a(1),x),(x,b(1)),(a(2),y),(y,b(3)). Change only the final b(3) to b(2). Trace through x,y rather than checking only individual sets; coupled p1/p2 causes remain explicit.
pending.consistent-shifted-overlap: PENDING compile/source positive control: INTEGER a(2),b(3); sets (a(1),b(2)),(a(2),b(3)). The offset is constant and adjacent units remain adjacent. Different extents or a nonzero offset alone are not errors. Any later value parent must first define every referenced INTEGER element and retain its separate effect owner.

review_rationale: Independent source review in doc/source_audits/batch_085.json reads both original 8.10.1.5 restrictions and their seven fine units. The two unnumbered prohibitions stay distinct: one storage unit shall not occur more than once in a storage sequence, and consecutive storage units shall not be made nonconsecutive. Both keep a context-dependent diagnostic obligation rather than a numbered-constraint reporting duty, and neither is downgraded to a definition. All eight facets remain pending source plans; no case, execution, oracle or fixture approval is created.
